newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume leaps to 2.18 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume leaps to 2.18 tonnes.

text.p: Istanbul gold exchange volume surged to 2,182 kilos on Friday from Thursday's 344 kilos as free market demand picked up on lower prices in pre-holiday trade and as banks became heavily involved in arbitrage deals, dealers said.
Daily volume was the second highest since a record 2,570 kilos on January 8.
Turkish markets have closed for a Moslem holiday and will reopen on February 12.

Gold closed sharply lower at $340.70 an ounce against Thursday's $345.00 in line with world trends, but it firmed in lira terms to 1,299,500 per gram from Thursday's 1,298,000 lira due to a weak lira.
The lira ended at 117,850 to the dollar, against Thursday's 117,080, due to a firmer dollar/mark parity.
Dealers said the four-day holiday also boosted free market demand.
They said the price fall in dollar terms and rise in lira terms provided a good opportunity for banks to engage in arbitrage deals by buying gold in dollars and selling in lira.
The bulk of the day's trade -- 1,597 kilos -- was conducted in the morning session. Some 60 percent of total turnover was in lira terms.
